info.name: AI Customer Support API
info.description:
HTTP APIs for the TypeScript backend (`apps/api`).

**Setup**
1. Import this collection and `local.postman_environment.json`.
2. Select the **AI Customer Support — Local** environment.
3. Keep cookies enabled (Postman → Cookies). Login, email verify, and Google complete set `access_token` and `refresh_token` httpOnly cookies.

**Auth flow**
1. Register
2. Copy the verification token from the API logs (development console email) into `verificationToken`
3. Verify email (sets session cookies)
4. Call Get current user, Refresh, or Logout

Passwords must be at least 12 characters and include a letter and a number.

Google OAuth: Start Google sign-in → open `googleAuthorizationUrl` in a browser → after redirect, put the `code` query value into `googleLoginCode` → Complete Google sign-in.

**Organizations / RBAC**
Tenant routes require a session cookie and membership in that organization. Send `x-tenant-id` as the organization id (must match the path when both are present).
1. Create organization (saves `organizationId`)
2. Invite a teammate — copy `?token=` from the API logs into `invitationToken`
3. Preview invitation (public) then Accept invitation while signed in as `inviteEmail`
4. List members, change roles, audit logs

Roles: `owner`, `admin`, `agent`, `viewer`. Invite roles cannot be `owner`.

**Conversations**
Tenant routes under `/api/organizations/:organizationId/conversations`. Requires session cookies and `x-tenant-id`.
1. Create organization, then Create conversation (saves `conversationId`)
2. Send message, add tag, add internal note
3. Assign / unassign / assign available, change status, escalate
4. List/search with `q`, `status`, `assignedAgentId`, `tag`, pagination

**Tickets**
Tenant routes under `/api/organizations/:organizationId/tickets`, `/ticket-sla-policies`, and `/ticket-escalation-policies`. Requires `ticket.manage` (agent+).
1. Create a conversation, then Create ticket (optional `conversationId`; saves `ticketId`). SLA due dates apply from a matching policy or defaults.
2. Assign / unassign / assign available, change status (`open` → `pending` | `resolved` | `closed` | `escalated`), escalate (bumps priority).
3. Add notes and upload attachments (form-data `file`).
4. SLA policies: one per priority (`any`/`low`/`normal`/`high`/`urgent`). Escalation policies fire on overdue first response, overdue resolution, or unassigned time.
5. Evaluate now with `POST .../ticket-escalation-policies/evaluate` (also runs every 30s).
AI conversations: escalating a conversation (including widget/AI) opens a ticket if none is open. Tools `createTicket` / `updateTicket` persist through TypeScript (`POST .../tools/calls`).

**Automations**
Tenant routes under `/api/organizations/:organizationId/automations`, `/automation-jobs`, and `/automation-logs`. Manage requires `automation.manage` (admin+); list/get requires `automation.read` (agent+).
1. Create an event rule (`TicketCreated` + conditions) or a schedule (`every:{n}m`, `hourly:{mm}`, `daily:{HH:MM}`, `weekly:{0-6}:{HH:MM}` UTC).
2. Matching domain events enqueue idempotent jobs (`evt:{tenant}:{rule}:{eventId}`). Schedules enqueue `sch:{tenant}:{rule}:{slot}`.
3. The worker executes `record`, `http_request`, or `emit_event` with retries and exponential backoff. Duplicate idempotency keys are no-ops.
4. Inspect jobs and execution logs, retry `dead`/`skipped` jobs, or `POST .../automations/dispatch` to run due work now (also every 5s).
5. `POST .../automations/:ruleId/run` with `idempotencyKey` for a manual, idempotent enqueue.

**Analytics**
Tenant routes under `/api/organizations/:organizationId/analytics`. Requires `analytics.view` (viewer+, and agents). All queries are organization-scoped and run SQL aggregations (`COUNT`/`AVG`/`date_trunc`) over indexed `created_at` / `resolved_at` columns — never load full row sets.
1. Overview KPIs (`GET .../overview`): conversations, tickets, SLA, messages, customers, knowledge, widget sessions. Optional `from`, `to` (ISO-8601, default last 30 days, max 366), `granularity`, `channel`, `status`, `assignedAgentId`.
2. Time series (`GET .../timeseries`): `metrics` comma list (`conversations.created`, `tickets.created`, `messages.ai`, …) and `granularity` `hour` (max 14 days) / `day` / `week` / `month`. Missing buckets are filled with 0 (UTC).
3. Reports: `GET .../conversations`, `/tickets`, `/agents`, `/customers`.
4. CSV export: `GET .../exports/:report` where report is `overview` | `timeseries` | `conversations` | `tickets` | `agents` | `customers`. Returns `text/csv` with `Content-Disposition: attachment`.

**Notifications**
Tenant routes under `/api/organizations/:organizationId/notification-templates`, `/notifications`, `/notification-preferences`, `/notification-deliveries`, and `/notification-attempts`. Manage requires `notification.manage` (admin+); inbox, preferences, and delivery tracking require `notification.read` (viewer+).
1. Create a template (`email` / `in_app` / `sms` / `webhook`) with `{{variable}}` placeholders, a recipient type, and optional `recipientField` for event-driven sends.
2. Matching domain events enqueue idempotent deliveries (`evt:{tenant}:{template}:{eventId}:{recipient}`). Manual send: `POST .../notifications` with `idempotencyKey`.
3. Channel providers are abstracted (SMTP or console email, in-app inbox, console SMS, HTTPS webhook). Deliveries retry with exponential backoff; inspect attempts and retry `dead`/`skipped`.
4. Recipients opt out per event/channel (`*` mutes a channel). Default is opted in. In-app items land in `GET .../notifications/inbox`.
5. `POST .../notifications/dispatch` runs due work now (also every 5s).

**Billing**
Tenant routes under `/api/organizations/:organizationId/billing`. Catalog: `GET /api/billing/plans`. Provider webhooks: `POST /api/billing/webhooks/:provider` (public, HMAC for Stripe). Manage requires `billing.manage` (admin+); reads require `billing.read` (viewer+).
1. Creating an organization provisions a free/trial subscription. List plans, then Start checkout (`starter`/`growth`/`scale`) and Complete checkout (console) or wait for the Stripe webhook.
2. Usage is metered from domain events (`ConversationCreated`, `TicketCreated`, `MessageReceived` including `ai_replies`, knowledge uploads, seats) and `POST .../billing/usage`. Check remaining quota with `POST .../billing/quotas/check` (HTTP 402 when exceeded).
3. Issue invoices for the current period (plan + overage), pay or void them, and inspect payment methods.
4. Cancel at period end / resume, or `POST .../billing/renew` to close due periods (also every 30s).
Providers: `BILLING_PROVIDER=console` locally, `stripe` with `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.

**Security**
Tenant routes under `/api/organizations/:organizationId/security`. Reads require `security.read` (viewer+); mutations require `security.manage` (admin+).
1. Get/update the tenant security policy (IP allowlist toggle, MFA required flag, session idle timeout, max request bytes, per-minute rate limit, audit retention).
2. Manage CIDR IP allowlist entries. When enabled, requests to `/api/organizations/:organizationId/*` from non-matching IPs return 403 and are audited.
3. Isolated secret vault: create/list/get metadata, reveal (plaintext once, audited), rotate, revoke. Values are stored with AES-256-GCM (`SECURITY_ENCRYPTION_KEY`). Encrypt/decrypt arbitrary payloads with the same envelope format.
4. Security audit logs (`action`, `outcome`, `resourceType` filters) and current IP/tenant rate-limit windows.
Global controls on every `/api` response: secure headers (HSTS in production), JSON Content-Type enforcement, body-size limits, and Redis IP + tenant rate limits (`SECURITY_GLOBAL_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE`).

**Platform administration**
Privileged operators (not organization members) under `/api/platform`. Session cookies required. Roles: `owner`, `admin`, `operator`, `auditor`.
1. Set `PLATFORM_BOOTSTRAP_EMAIL` to a verified user, then `POST /api/platform/bootstrap` (or restart the API) to grant the first owner.
2. Grant/change/revoke operators. Only an owner can grant or revoke `owner`. The last owner cannot be revoked.
3. List/get tenants; suspend (`disabled`) or activate. Suspended tenants cannot be used (`ORGANIZATION_DISABLED`).
4. Feature flags (global + per-tenant overrides). Seeded keys: `ai_replies`, `widget`, `public_api`, `billing`, `knowledge_ingestion`, `automations`, `notifications`, `analytics`.
5. Operational health (`database`, `redis`, `ai_service`) and platform audit logs.
Permissions: `platform.operators.manage` (owner), `platform.tenants.manage` (operator+), `platform.feature_flags.manage` (admin+), `platform.health.read` / `platform.audit.view` (auditor+).

**Customers / commerce lookup**
Tenant routes under `/api/organizations/:organizationId/customers`, `/products`, `/orders`, `/shipments`, and `/returns`. Writes require `customer.manage` (admin+). Reads and AI lookup tools require `customer.read` (viewer+). Every query includes the organization id — records never leak across tenants. Register a customer, then product, order, shipment, and return. AI tools `getCustomerDetails`, `getProductDetails`, `getOrderDetails`, `getShipmentDetails`, and `getReturnDetails` are executed by TypeScript (`POST .../tools/calls`).

**Realtime, presence, and escalation rules**
WebSocket: `GET {{wsUrl}}/api/organizations/:organizationId/realtime?lastEventId=&access_token=` (session cookie or `access_token` query). On connect the server sends `connected`, missed `event`s, and `presence.snapshot`. Client messages: `heartbeat`, `resume`, `presence.set`, `subscribe` / `unsubscribe`.
HTTP catch-up: `GET .../realtime/events?after=`.
Presence: list/set/heartbeat under `/agents/presence`.
Escalation rules: CRUD + `POST .../evaluate`. Assign available picks an online owner/admin/agent (round-robin).

**Onboarding / knowledge**
Tenant routes under `/api/organizations/:organizationId/onboarding`, `/knowledge/sources`, and `/knowledge/documents`. Requires session cookies and `x-tenant-id`.
1. Create organization, then Run onboarding setup (saves profile, tones, agent settings; optional knowledge sources)
2. Or step through Generate business profile → Generate tone presets → Select tone → Generate agent settings
3. Register extra knowledge sources (URL, help center, sitemap, text, file)
4. Add documents: article/URL JSON, or upload PDF/DOCX — TypeScript owns lifecycle; Python indexes for RAG
5. List documents, reindex, or delete (delete also drops vector index entries)
Permissions: `organization.update` for LLM setup (admin+), `knowledge.manage` to register sources and documents (agent+), `organization.read` to view.

**Python AI service**
Folder `Python AI service` calls `apps/ai` directly (`{{aiServiceUrl}}`, default http://localhost:8000) for local RAG/onboarding debugging. Production clients use the TypeScript API only.

Permissions: `conversation.read` (viewer+), `conversation.write` (agent+), `conversation.assign`, `conversation.escalate`.
Status: `open` → `pending` | `resolved` | `closed` | `escalated`. Closed conversations reject new messages until reopened.

**Widget**
Staff: `GET/PATCH /api/organizations/:organizationId/widget` and `POST .../rotate-key` (session cookies + `x-tenant-id`). Public embed: `GET /api/widget/:publicKey/config`, then `POST /api/widget/:publicKey/sessions` (anonymous or email/name). Send `sessionToken` as `Authorization: Bearer` on `/api/widget/sessions/*` and `/api/widget/conversations*`.
1. Get widget configuration (saves `widgetPublicKey`)
2. Create anonymous session (saves `widgetSessionToken`) or Create customer session
3. Start widget conversation (saves `widgetConversationId`)
4. Send message, or stream AI reply (`text/event-stream`)
5. Upload attachment (form-data `file`) then send `attachmentIds`
Tenant isolation: sessions, conversations, attachments, and AI calls are scoped to the organization behind the public key. Allowed origins are enforced when configured.

**Tools and integrations**
Python proposes allowlisted tool calls (`POST .../tools/propose`); TypeScript schema-validates, authorizes, executes, and audits (`POST .../tools/calls`). Tenant credentials and OAuth connectors are encrypted per organization. Mutating tools never run in Python. Permission: `integration.manage` (admin+) for secrets.

**Public API v1**
Versioned REST at `/api/v1` (OpenAPI `/api/v1/openapi.json`, docs `/api/v1/docs`). Create API keys, HMAC-signed webhooks, inbound OAuth apps, and inspect the connector catalog. Programmatic auth: `Authorization: Bearer acs_live_…` or `X-API-Key`. Existing dashboard routes remain under `/api`.

request.description: Process liveness. Returns 200 even if PostgreSQL or Redis are down.
Infrastructure readiness for PostgreSQL and Redis. 200 when both are up, 503 otherwise.
Creates an unverified account and sends a verification email. In development the verify URL is logged by the console email adapter. Does not set session cookies.
Sends a new verification link if an unverified password account exists. Always returns a generic success message.
Consumes the email verification token from the link (`?token=`). Sets `access_token` and `refresh_token` cookies and returns the verified user.
Password login. Email must already be verified. Sets `access_token` and `refresh_token` cookies. Rate limited per IP and email.
Returns the authenticated user. Requires a valid `access_token` cookie or `Authorization: Bearer` access token.
Rotates the refresh token using the `refresh_token` cookie and issues a new access cookie. Reusing a previous refresh token revokes the whole family.
Revokes the current refresh session and clears auth cookies. Returns 204.
Requests a password reset email. Always returns a generic success message. In development the reset URL is logged by the console email adapter — copy `?token=` into `resetToken`.
Sets a new password, revokes all refresh sessions, and clears cookies. Then sign in with `newPassword`.
Returns a Google authorization URL with PKCE. Open `authorizationUrl` in a browser. Requires `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`, and `GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI`.

Google redirects here after consent. The API exchanges the OAuth code, then redirects to the web app with a one-time login code. Normally invoked by Google, not Postman. Disable auto-follow redirects to inspect the Location header.
Exchanges the one-time login code from `/auth/callback?code=` for session cookies. The code is single-use and expires quickly.

item.name: Organizations
item.description: Multi-tenant workspaces. Create/list do not need `x-tenant-id`. All `/:organizationId` routes authenticate, resolve tenant membership, and check RBAC. The path id must match `x-tenant-id` when the header is sent.

request.description: Creates an organization and makes the current user the owner. Requires a session cookie. 201 `{ organization }` including `membership.role` and `membership.permissions`.
Lists organizations the authenticated user belongs to, with their role and permissions. Does not include other tenants.
Returns the organization and the caller's membership. Requires `organization.read`. Cross-tenant ids return 403 `UNAUTHORIZED_ORGANIZATION_ACCESS`.
Updates name and/or slug. Requires `organization.update` (owner or admin). Slug must be 3–48 lowercase letters, numbers, or hyphens.
Removes the current user from the organization. The last owner cannot leave (409 `LAST_OWNER`). Returns 204.
Tenant-scoped member list. Requires `organization.read`. Never returns another organization's members.

exec: const other = members.find((member) => member.userId !== members.find((item) => item.role === 'owner')?.userId) || members[0];

request.description: Changes another member's role. Requires `organization.members.manage`. You cannot change your own role. Only an owner can grant or revoke `owner`. Role: `owner` | `admin` | `agent` | `viewer`.
Removes another member. Requires `organization.members.manage`. Cannot remove yourself (use Leave) or the last owner. Returns 204.

Sends a team invitation. Requires `organization.invitations.manage`. Role must be `admin`, `agent`, or `viewer` (not `owner`). In development the accept URL is logged — copy `?token=` into `invitationToken`.
Lists pending invitations for this tenant. Requires `organization.invitations.manage`.
Public preview of an invitation (organization name, invited email, role, expiry). No auth. Invalid or expired tokens return 400 `INVALID_INVITATION_TOKEN`.
Accepts the invitation for the signed-in user. The session email must match the invited address. Does not use `x-tenant-id` — tenant comes from the invitation.
Revokes a pending invitation. Requires `organization.invitations.manage`. Returns 204.

Tenant-scoped audit log. Requires `organization.audit.view` (owner or admin). Query: `page` (min 1), `pageSize` (1–100). Actions include `organization.created`, `organization.member.invited`, `organization.invitation.accepted`, `organization.member.role_changed`.

Creates an open conversation for a customer. Requires `conversation.write`. Optional: subject, channel (`web` | `email` | `api`), tags, assignedAgentId, initialMessage, initialMessageAuthor (`customer` | `agent`).
Paginated inbox search. Requires `conversation.read`. Query: `page`, `pageSize` (1–100), `q` (subject, customer, tags, message body), `status`, `assignedAgentId` (user id or `unassigned`), `tag`.
Loads one tenant-scoped conversation with tags and assignee. Requires `conversation.read`.
Assigns an active owner, admin, or agent in this organization. Requires `conversation.assign`.
Assigns the conversation to the next online owner, admin, or agent (round-robin). Requires `conversation.assign`. Returns 409 `NO_AVAILABLE_AGENT` when nobody is online.
Clears the assignee. Requires `conversation.assign`.

Transitions status. Requires `conversation.write`. Allowed: `open`, `pending`, `resolved`, `closed`. Use Escalate for `escalated`. Closed conversations cannot accept messages until reopened to `open`.
Escalates an `open` or `pending` conversation. Requires `conversation.escalate`. Optional reason (max 500).
Adds a tag (1–32 lowercase letters, numbers, or hyphens; max 20 tags). Requires `conversation.write`.
Removes a tag from the conversation. Requires `conversation.write`.
Adds a message. Requires `conversation.write`. `authorType` defaults to `agent` (use `customer` to log a customer reply). Closed conversations return 409 `CONVERSATION_CLOSED`.
Paginated messages in chronological order. Requires `conversation.read`.
Adds an internal note (not a customer-visible message). Requires `conversation.write`.
Paginated internal notes. Requires `conversation.read`.

Opens a tenant-scoped ticket. Requires `ticket.manage`. Optional `conversationId` links it to a conversation (one open ticket per conversation). SLA due dates are applied from a matching SLA policy or platform defaults.
Tenant-scoped ticket search. Requires `ticket.manage`. Filter with `status`, `priority`, `assignedAgentId` (`unassigned` or a UUID), `conversationId`, `slaBreached=true|false`, or `q`.
Load one ticket including SLA timers. Requires `ticket.manage`. Lookup is always scoped to the path organization.
Lifecycle transition: open → pending | resolved | closed | escalated. Pending pauses resolution SLA. Resolved/closed records first response. Requires `ticket.manage`.
Assign to an active owner/admin/agent in the organization. Records first response. Requires `ticket.manage`.
Round-robin assign an online owner/admin/agent. Requires `ticket.manage`.
Clear the assignee. Requires `ticket.manage`.
Mark the ticket escalated and bump priority. Requires `ticket.manage`.
Internal note on a ticket. Records first response. Requires `ticket.manage`.
Paginated internal notes. Requires `ticket.manage`.
Upload PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, PDF, or plain text (max 5MB). Requires `ticket.manage`.

formdata.description: Select a local file before sending.

request.description: Download an attachment. Requires `ticket.manage`. Tenant-scoped; never returns another organization's file.
Define first-response and resolution targets for a priority (`any`, `low`, `normal`, `high`, `urgent`). One policy per priority per organization. Requires `ticket.manage`.
List tenant SLA policies. Requires `ticket.manage`.
Update name, enabled flag, priority, or timer minutes. Requires `ticket.manage`.
Remove an SLA policy. Existing tickets keep their already-computed due dates. Requires `ticket.manage`.

Triggers: `first_response_overdue`, `resolution_overdue`, `unassigned_for` (requires `triggerMinutes`). Actions: `mark_escalated`, `bump_priority`, `unassign`, `assign_available`, `escalate_and_unassign`. Requires `ticket.manage`.
List tenant ticket escalation policies. Requires `ticket.manage`.
Update trigger, action, or enabled flag. Requires `ticket.manage`.
Run SLA timers and matching escalation policies for this organization now. Also runs on a 30s background interval. Requires `ticket.manage`.
Remove a ticket escalation policy. Requires `ticket.manage`.
AI `createTicket` is authorized and executed in TypeScript. Opens a real ticket on the conversation (idempotent if one is already open). Requires `ticket.manage`.
AI `updateTicket` changes status and/or adds a note. Mutating tools never run in Python. Requires `ticket.manage`.

Create a tenant-scoped automation rule that fires on a domain event. Requires `automation.manage` (admin+). Conditions use dotted payload fields (`eq`, `neq`, `contains`, `exists`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `in`, `not_in`). Actions: `record`, `http_request`, or `emit_event`. Jobs are queued with retries, exponential backoff, and an idempotency key of `evt:{tenant}:{rule}:{eventId}`.

body.raw:
{
  "name": "Log AI-opened tickets",
  "description": "Record when an AI conversation opens a ticket",
  "enabled": true,
  "triggerType": "event",
  "eventName": "TicketCreated",
  "match": "all",
  "conditions": [
    { "field": "source", "operator": "eq", "value": "ai_conversation" }
  ],
  "actionType": "record",
  "action": { "message": "AI conversation opened a ticket" },
  "maxAttempts": 3,
  "backoffMs": 2000,
  "priority": 100
}

request.description: Create a scheduled rule. `schedule` is `every:{n}m`, `hourly:{mm}`, `daily:{HH:MM}`, or `weekly:{0-6}:{HH:MM}` (UTC). The dispatcher runs every 5s and enqueues due jobs with idempotency key `sch:{tenant}:{rule}:{slot}`.
List automation rules for the organization. Requires `automation.read` (agent+).
Load one rule including conditions, action, retry policy, and next scheduled run. Lookup is tenant-scoped.
Update name, conditions, action, retry policy, or trigger. Requires `automation.manage`.
Enable a rule. Scheduled rules compute the next run from now.
Disable a rule so events and schedules no longer enqueue jobs.
Manually enqueue a job. Repeat with the same `idempotencyKey` returns the existing job (`created: false`). Requires `automation.manage`.
List queued and completed jobs for one rule.
List execution attempts for one rule (started, succeeded, failed, skipped).
Delete a rule and cascade its jobs and logs. Requires `automation.manage`.
Enqueue due scheduled rules and pending retries now. The same loop also runs every 5s. Requires `automation.manage`.
Tenant-scoped job search. Filter with `ruleId` and `status` (`pending`, `running`, `succeeded`, `skipped`, `dead`).
Load one job including attempt count, last error, and idempotency key.
Re-queue a `dead` or `skipped` job. Failed jobs with remaining attempts retry automatically with exponential backoff.
List execution attempts. Filter with `ruleId`, `jobId`, and `status` (`started`, `succeeded`, `failed`, `skipped`). Each attempt stores input/output snapshots.

Tenant-scoped KPI snapshot: conversations, tickets (including SLA), messages, customers, knowledge, and widget sessions. Aggregated in PostgreSQL with `organization_id` predicates. Requires `analytics.view`. Omit `from`/`to` for the last 30 days (UTC). Max range 366 days. Optional filters: `channel`, `status`, `assignedAgentId`.

UTC time-series via `date_trunc`. `granularity`: `hour` (max 14 days), `day`, `week`, or `month`. `metrics` is a comma list: `conversations.created`, `conversations.resolved`, `tickets.created`, `tickets.resolved`, `tickets.sla_breached`, `messages.created`, `messages.customer`, `messages.agent`, `messages.ai`, `customers.created`, `widget.sessions_created`. Empty buckets are filled with 0.
Conversation volume in the period: created count, status/channel/tag breakdowns, unassigned count, and average first-response seconds (first agent/AI message via indexed LATERAL lookup).

Ticket volume in the period: created, resolved (`resolved_at` in range), SLA breaches (`sla_breached_at` in range), status/priority/source breakdowns, unassigned, and average first-response / resolution seconds.
Per-agent assigned/resolved conversations and tickets in the period, plus average ticket first-response and resolution times. Capped at 200 agents. Lookup is tenant-scoped.
New customers in the period, distinct emails with conversations, and top 50 customers by conversation volume (with ticket counts and last seen).
Download the overview report as CSV (`Content-Disposition: attachment`). Requires `analytics.view`. Other report names: `timeseries`, `conversations`, `tickets`, `agents`, `customers`.
CSV of metric,bucket,value rows for the requested time series.
CSV of conversation aggregations (counts, status/channel/tag breakdowns, first-response average).
CSV of ticket aggregations including SLA breaches and average first-response / resolution times.
CSV with one row per agent: assigned/resolved conversations and tickets plus averages.
CSV of new-customer counts plus the top customers by conversation volume.

Create a tenant-scoped notification template. Placeholders use `{{variable}}` (dotted paths allowed). `recipientField` is read from matching domain-event payloads for event-driven sends. Requires `notification.manage` (admin+). Channels: `email`, `in_app`, `sms`, `webhook`. Retry policy defaults to 5 attempts with 2s exponential backoff.

body.raw:
{
  "name": "Ticket assigned",
  "slug": "ticket-assigned-email",
  "channel": "email",
  "eventType": "TicketAssigned",
  "subject": "Ticket assigned",
  "body": "A ticket was assigned to you. Use template placeholders like double-brace field names (ticketId, assigneeName, subject).",
  "recipientType": "email",
  "recipientField": "assigneeEmail",
  "enabled": true,
  "maxAttempts": 5,
  "backoffMs": 2000
}

request.description: In-app templates deliver to a user UUID (`recipientType: user`) and write an inbox item. Event matching uses `recipientField` (for example `assignedAgentId`).

body.raw:
{
  "name": "Ticket assigned in-app",
  "slug": "ticket-assigned-in-app",
  "channel": "in_app",
  "eventType": "TicketAssigned",
  "subject": "Ticket assigned",
  "body": "A ticket was assigned to you.",
  "recipientType": "user",
  "recipientField": "assignedAgentId",
  "enabled": true
}

request.description: List notification templates for the organization. Requires `notification.read` (viewer+).
Load one template including channel, event type, body, recipient mapping, and retry policy. Lookup is tenant-scoped.
Update name, body, recipient mapping, or retry policy. Requires `notification.manage`.
Delete a template. Existing deliveries keep a null templateId. Requires `notification.manage`.

Enqueue a delivery from a template. Repeat with the same `idempotencyKey` returns the existing delivery (`created: false`). Honors recipient preferences unless `ignorePreferences` is true. Requires `notification.manage`.
Enqueue an ad-hoc notification without a template. `channel` and `body` are required. Providers: SMTP when `SMTP_URL` is set, otherwise the development console logger.
Enqueue an in-app notification to a member user id (`assignedAgentId` from Assign conversation). On delivery the inbox item is created for that user.
Enqueue pending and stale sending deliveries now. The worker also runs every 5s. Requires `notification.manage`.
List the current member's channel preferences. Missing rows mean opted in. `eventType` of `*` mutes an entire channel. Requires `notification.read`.
Create or update the current member's preferences. Opt out of email for `TicketAssigned`, or mute a channel with `eventType: "*"`.
Admins can list another recipient's preferences (`subjectType` + `subjectKey`). Requires `notification.manage` when the subject is not the current user.
List queued and completed deliveries. Filter with `templateId`, `status` (`pending`, `sending`, `delivered`, `skipped`, `dead`), `channel`, and `recipient`. Requires `notification.read`.
Load one delivery including rendered body, provider, attempt count, and tracking timestamps. Lookup is tenant-scoped.
Re-queue a `dead` or `skipped` delivery. Requires `notification.manage`.
List provider attempts for one delivery (`started`, `delivered`, `failed`, `skipped`) with provider message ids.
List delivery attempts across the organization. Filter with `deliveryId` and `status`.
List in-app notifications for the current member. Add `unreadOnly=true` to hide read items. Returns `unreadCount`. Requires `notification.read`.
Mark one inbox item as read. Only the recipient can update their inbox.
Mark every unread inbox item for the current member as read. Returns `{ updated }`.
Public catalog of active subscription plans (`free`, `starter`, `growth`, `scale`) with included quotas and overage rates. Requires a session cookie. Saves `billingPlanSlug` from the first paid plan.
Current organization subscription. Created automatically on `OrganizationCreated` (free/trial). Requires `billing.read` (viewer+).
Start a paid-plan checkout. Console provider returns a session with no hosted URL — complete it with Complete checkout. Stripe returns a Checkout URL. Requires `billing.manage` (admin+).
Activates the paid plan for a pending console checkout session. Stripe activations arrive via `POST /api/billing/webhooks/stripe` instead.
Switch the active subscription to another catalog plan. Paid Stripe subscriptions also update the provider.
Schedule cancellation at the end of the current period (`immediately: false`) or cancel now.
Undo a pending cancel-at-period-end. Fully canceled subscriptions must start a new checkout.
Current-period usage vs included quotas for conversations, AI replies, seats, knowledge documents, tickets, and messages. Event metering is automatic. Requires `billing.read`.
Same payload as Get usage — remaining included units and overage for the current period.
Ask whether `quantity` of a metric is allowed under the current plan and subscription status. `allowed: false` when the subscription is inactive or the included quota would be exceeded.
Manually record metered usage. Duplicate `idempotencyKey` values are no-ops. `enforceQuota` defaults to true (HTTP 402 `QUOTA_EXCEEDED`). Requires `billing.manage`.
Tenant-scoped invoices. Filter with `status` (`draft` | `open` | `paid` | `void` | `uncollectible`). Requires `billing.read`.
Finalize an invoice for the current (or supplied) billing period: plan fee plus usage overage. Duplicate periods return 409. $0 invoices are marked paid. Requires `billing.manage`.
Invoice header and line items (plan, usage overage, credits, tax).
Mark an open invoice paid (console/local). Reactivates `past_due` / `unpaid` subscriptions. Stripe invoice.paid webhooks do the same.
Void an unpaid invoice. Paid invoices cannot be voided.
Stored payment methods for the organization (brand, last four). Populated after checkout completion or a provider webhook.

Inbound payment-provider webhook (no session cookie). Console events are accepted unsigned when `BILLING_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is empty. Stripe uses `POST /api/billing/webhooks/stripe` with `Stripe-Signature`. Events are idempotent on `id`. Types: `checkout.session.completed`, `customer.subscription.updated`, `customer.subscription.deleted`, `invoice.paid`, `invoice.payment_failed`.
Issue invoices and advance periods for subscriptions whose `currentPeriodEnd` is due (also runs every 30s). Cancel-at-period-end subscriptions are canceled. Requires `billing.manage`.

Current tenant security policy (IP allowlist, MFA required, session idle timeout, max request bytes, rate limit, audit retention). Provisioned on `OrganizationCreated`. Requires `security.read` (viewer+).

Update tenant security controls. Enabling `ipAllowlistEnabled` without matching CIDR entries denies all tenant-scoped requests. Requires `security.manage` (admin+). Audited as `security.policy.updated`.
CIDR entries allowed when the policy IP allowlist is enabled. IPv4 prefixes /8–/32 and IPv6 /32–/128. Requires `security.read`.
Add a CIDR or host address to the allowlist (bare IPv4 becomes /32). Requires `security.manage`. Saves `securityIpEntryId`.
Remove a CIDR entry. Requires `security.manage`. Audited as `security.ip_allowlist.removed`.
Metadata for isolated tenant secrets. Ciphertext and plaintext are never listed. Requires `security.read`.

Store a secret encrypted with AES-256-GCM. `name` is a lowercase identifier; `purpose` is `api_credential` | `webhook` | `integration` | `encryption` | `other`. Requires `security.manage`. Saves `securitySecretId`.
Secret metadata only (no plaintext). Requires `security.read`.
Decrypt and return plaintext once. Heavily audited (`security.secret.revealed`). Requires `security.manage`.
Re-encrypt with a new plaintext. Previous ciphertext is replaced. Requires `security.manage`.
Revoke a secret so it can no longer be revealed. Requires `security.manage`.

Encrypt arbitrary plaintext with the tenant AES-256-GCM master key. Returns `{ algorithm, keyVersion, ciphertext, nonce }`. Requires `security.manage`. Saves envelope fields for Decrypt payload. Plaintext is never written to audit logs.
Decrypt an envelope produced by Encrypt payload or the secret vault. Requires `security.manage`. Audited without returning ciphertext in logs.

Tenant security audit trail (policy changes, secret access, IP allowlist, encrypt/decrypt, authorization denials). Filter by `action`, `outcome` (`success` | `denied` | `failure`), `resourceType`. Requires `security.read`. Sensitive metadata keys are redacted.

Current IP (global `SECURITY_GLOBAL_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE`) and tenant (`policy.rateLimitPerMinute`) sliding windows: used, remaining, resetAt. Requires `security.read`. Exceeding either limit returns HTTP 429 with `Retry-After`.
Returns the authenticated user's platform operator profile and permissions. 403 if they are not an active operator. Does not require a tenant header.

Grants `owner` to the authenticated user when no operators exist and their email matches `PLATFORM_BOOTSTRAP_EMAIL`. Also runs on API start. 409 when operators already exist or bootstrap is not configured.
Lists platform operators. Requires `platform.operators.read` (auditor+). Query: `includeRevoked`.

Grants platform access to an existing verified user. Requires `platform.operators.manage` (owner). Role: `owner` | `admin` | `operator` | `auditor`. Only an owner can grant `owner`. Reinstates a previously revoked operator.
Changes another operator's role. Requires `platform.operators.manage`. You cannot change your own role. Only an owner can grant or revoke `owner`. The last owner cannot be demoted.
Revokes platform access. Requires `platform.operators.manage`. You cannot revoke yourself or the last owner. Audited as `platform.operator.revoked`.
Lists all organizations with member counts. Requires `platform.tenants.read` (auditor+). Query: `page`, `pageSize`, `status`, `q`.
Tenant summary for platform operators. Requires `platform.tenants.read`.

Disables the organization. Members receive 403 `ORGANIZATION_DISABLED` on tenant routes until activate. Requires `platform.tenants.manage` (operator+). Idempotent if already disabled. Audited as `platform.tenant.suspended`.
Re-enables a suspended organization. Requires `platform.tenants.manage`. Idempotent if already active. Audited as `platform.tenant.activated`.

Global flags with tenant overrides. Seeded on API start: `ai_replies`, `widget`, `public_api`, `billing`, `knowledge_ingestion`, `automations`, `notifications`, `analytics`. Requires `platform.feature_flags.read`.
Creates a flag. Key must start with a letter and use lowercase letters, numbers, or underscores (2–64). Requires `platform.feature_flags.manage` (admin+).
Flag metadata and tenant overrides. Requires `platform.feature_flags.read`.
Updates global enabled state and/or description. Requires `platform.feature_flags.manage`. Audited as `platform.feature_flag.updated`.

Removes a tenant override so the global value applies. Requires `platform.feature_flags.manage`.
Deletes a flag and its overrides. Requires `platform.feature_flags.manage`. Audited as `platform.feature_flag.deleted`.

Operator health for PostgreSQL, Redis, and the Python AI service, with latency. `ok` when all are up, `degraded` when a non-database check is down, `unavailable` when the database is down (HTTP 503). Requires `platform.health.read` (auditor+). Distinct from public `GET /health` and `GET /ready`.

Platform-wide operational audit trail. Requires `platform.audit.view` (auditor+). Query: `page`, `pageSize`, `action`, `outcome` (`success` | `denied` | `failure`), `resourceType`, `organizationId`, `actorId`. Actions include `platform.operator.granted`, `platform.tenant.suspended`, `platform.feature_flag.updated`.

Load one customer by id. Requires `customer.read`. Lookup is always scoped to the path organization.

Load one product by id. Requires `customer.read`.

Load one order by internal id or use the same path with `{{externalOrderId}}`. Requires `customer.read`.
Creates a tenant-scoped shipment for an existing order. Requires `customer.manage`. Tracking numbers are unique per organization.
Tenant-scoped shipment search. Requires `customer.read`. Filter with `orderId` or `trackingNumber`.
Load one shipment by id. Requires `customer.read`.
Creates a tenant-scoped return for an existing order. Requires `customer.manage`.
Tenant-scoped return search. Requires `customer.read`. Filter with `orderId`.
Load one return by id. Requires `customer.read`.

Authorized tenant-scoped product lookup tool. Requires `customer.read`.

Authorized tenant-scoped shipment lookup tool. Requires `customer.read`.
Authorized tenant-scoped return lookup tool. Requires `customer.read`.

Creates a tenant rule. Requires `conversation.escalate`.

Actions: `escalate`, `escalate_and_unassign`, `assign_available` (falls back to escalate if nobody is online).

Events: `conversation.created` | `message_received` | `message_sent` | `status_changed` | `escalated` | `assigned` | `unassigned` | `note_added` | `agent.presence_changed`.

`{"type":"heartbeat"}`

Allowlisted tool catalog with JSON schemas, permissions, and retry policy. Requires `organization.read`.

Tenant-scoped tool audit trail. Requires `organization.audit.view` or `integration.manage`.
Send authorized tool results back to Python for a follow-up reply. Python does not mutate tickets or conversations.
Store a tenant-scoped API key or bearer secret (AES-256-GCM). Secret is never returned. Requires `integration.manage`.
Lists credentials with last-four only. Requires `integration.manage`.
Revokes a tenant credential. Requires `integration.manage`.
Register tenant OAuth client settings. Client secret is encrypted at rest. Requires `integration.manage`.
Lists OAuth connectors without tokens. Requires `integration.manage`.
Starts PKCE authorization. Open `authorizationUrl`, then complete with code+state.

Browser callback. State is one-time and tenant-scoped in Redis.

item.name: Public API v1
item.description:
Versioned REST API at `/api/v1`. Authenticate with session cookies, `Authorization: Bearer {{apiKey}}`, or `X-API-Key`. Management routes also exist under `/api/organizations/:id/...`. Responses include `X-API-Version: v1`.

**Setup**
1. Create organization and sign in (session cookies).
2. Create API key (saves `apiKey` once — copy it).
3. Create webhook, inspect delivery logs, verify HMAC signatures, then check API usage.

Webhook signatures: `X-Webhook-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex>` is HMAC-SHA256 of `{timestamp}.{rawBody}` using the subscription secret. Failed deliveries retry automatically (1m, 5m, 30m, 2h, 8h; max 5 attempts) or via Retry / Dispatch due retries.
OAuth: PKCE S256. Approve authorization (session) then Exchange token (client secret).

request.description: Unversioned discovery for the public API. Returns `v1`, schema version, and documentation URLs.
Machine-readable OpenAPI 3.1 document for `/api/v1`.
Swagger UI for the public API.
Returns auth kind (`session`, `api_key`, or `oauth_token`) and granted scopes. Send the API key as Bearer or X-API-Key to verify programmatic access.
Creates a tenant API key. `token` (`acs_live_…`) is shown once. Requires `integration.manage`. Rate-limited.
Lists keys with prefix and last-used time. Secrets are never returned.
Revokes a key. Requires `integration.manage`.
Subscribe to tenant events. `secret` is shown once. Deliveries POST JSON with `X-Webhook-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hmac-sha256>`. HTTPS required (localhost HTTP allowed outside production).
Lists subscriptions with secret last-four only.
Fetch one subscription.
Update URL, events, description, or pause (`status`: `active` | `paused`).
Issues a new signing secret. Shown once.
Delivery audit trail for this subscription. Status is `pending`, `succeeded`, `failed` (will retry), or `abandoned` (max attempts). Saves `webhookDeliveryId`.
Single delivery with stored event payload, attempt count, next retry time, and terminal status. Requires `integration.manage`.
Per-attempt delivery log: HTTP status, duration, `X-Webhook-Signature` header (`t=<unix>,v1=<hex>`), timestamp, error, and response preview. Saves `webhookSignatureHeader` from the latest attempt.

Validates `X-Webhook-Signature` against the stored subscription secret. HMAC-SHA256 of `{timestamp}.{rawBody}`; timestamp must be within `toleranceSeconds` (default 300). Requires `integration.manage`.
Retries failed deliveries whose `nextAttemptAt` is due. The API also runs this on a 5s interval. Exponential backoff: 1m, 5m, 30m, 2h, 8h; abandoned after 5 attempts. Requires `integration.manage`.
Re-sign and re-POST a stored payload.
Disables the subscription.

Aggregated `/api/v1` traffic for the last 7 days (override with `from` / `to`): totals, errors, average latency, and breakdowns by route, status class, auth kind, and day. Requires `integration.manage` or `organization.audit.view`. Session and API-key calls under `/api/v1` are recorded (docs/version endpoints are skipped).
Paginated request log. Filter with `method`, `route`, `statusCode`, `authKind` (`session` | `api_key` | `oauth_token`), `credentialId`, `from`, `to`. Paths are stored with UUIDs replaced by `{id}`.
Available HTTP API-key and OAuth connector types (Shopify, Stripe, Zendesk, custom).
Unified view of HTTP credentials and outbound OAuth connectors.
Versioned alias of the allowlisted tool catalog.
Registers an inbound OAuth 2.1 app. `clientSecret` (`acs_oas_…`) is shown once. Redirect URIs must be https (localhost HTTP allowed outside production).
Lists apps without client secrets.
Revokes the client. Requires `integration.manage`.
Session-authenticated consent details for an OAuth app. PKCE S256 required.
Issues a one-time authorization code and returns `redirectUrl`. Session required. Copy `code` from the redirect into `oauthAuthCode`.
Public token endpoint. `grantType`: `authorization_code` or `refresh_token`. Rate-limited by IP.
Rotate access and refresh tokens.

item.name: Python AI service
item.description: Direct calls to `apps/ai` (FastAPI) for local debugging. The web app never calls this service — production traffic goes TypeScript API → Python. Send `x-tenant-id` (use the organization id). Ingestion and retrieve are tenant-scoped.

request.description: Python AI process liveness. Returns `{ status: 'ok', service: 'ai' }`.
LLM business-profile generation. Requires tenant header. Prefer the TypeScript onboarding routes in production.
Generates tone presets from a business profile payload.
Generates agent settings from a business profile and selected tone.
Runs profile + tones + agent settings in one call.
Indexes an article into the vector store (in-memory or pgvector). Tenant-scoped. Prefer TypeScript `POST .../knowledge/documents` which owns lifecycle.
Hybrid keyword + vector retrieval with optional metadata filters, rerank, citations, and configurable `topK` (1–20).
Removes tenant-scoped vectors for a document id. Prefer TypeScript delete-document which also updates lifecycle.
Classifies a visitor message (greeting, question, complaint, escalation, …) with input guardrails. Tenant header required. Prefer TypeScript `AIServicePort.detectIntent` in production.

Full orchestration: intent, model route, RAG context, guardrails, retries/fallbacks, and a structured reply. Tenant header required. Prefer TypeScript `AIServicePort.orchestrateSupportTurn` in production.
Allowlisted tool schemas. Prefer TypeScript `GET /api/organizations/:id/tools` in production.
Python proposes schema-validated tool calls. It never executes them. Tenant header required.
Continue generation after TypeScript executed tools. Tenant header required.
SSE support reply with RAG context and citations on the `done` event. Optional `topK` and `retrieval` filters. Prefer the widget stream on the TypeScript API.
